newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates firm despite weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates firm despite weak demand.

text.p: Croatian money market trade was quiet on Friday with creditors reluctant to cut rates despite relatively weak demand for kuna, dealers said.
"Nevertheless, some five million kuna in demand was not met as some banks refused to increase their placements or turned down certain borrowers," one dealer said.
The morning deals of only 11.5 million kuna left a large suplus in supply for the second day running.
But the day's total volume was expected to be higher after matured loans have been renewed.
Interbank rates ranged between 10.5 percent for call money and 13-15 percent for short-term funds.
Some 58 million kuna were sold in Thursday's overnight trade, of which 50 million went to one bank for statutory reserves. The rest went for squaring shortages at two other banks.

Banking sector liquidity has improved since the central bank eased the reserve requirement by one percentage point this month. The bank conducted no intervention this week after injecting funds to help banks several times over the past month. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
